title: Use every GPU and CPU the cluster has
description: Serves "Growing is adding machines.". What JS-170 (the first slice: Intel VAAPI/QSV) leaves, under rule: NVIDIA NVENC and AMD VAAPI workers, hardware decoding for processor-encoded streams, and outputs above 1080 lines. fMP4 can't splice across encoder families (spikes/seam: x264 spliced with NVENC lost half the frames), so each stream keeps one family, and its helpers (JS-024) and failover stay in it.
acceptanceCriteria: Design reviewed before building: how a stream's family is chosen among several hardware families and the processor; what a viewer sees when the last worker of their stream's family is lost mid-film (as JS-170 settled it, or briefed); whether a copy and a re-encode share one slot pool; and whether a GPU family re-encodes above 1080 lines, from JS-148's figures.

NVIDIA NVENC and AMD VAAPI workers detect by a bounded real test of each stage at start, with nothing configured, and choose per job by rule (the same picture within its bound, 1.2 times real time measured, within twice x264's bytes, then the least processor; the processor otherwise, logged and counted with its reason). A node with no GPU runs exactly as before.

A new stream gets a hardware family when a worker of it has room and the processor otherwise; the family stays in the spec hash; helpers and failover stay in the family; a seek, a restart and a helper's chunk splice in Octave (or, until JS-190 and JS-150, the native browser check) on each family.
Hardware decoding for processor-encoded streams only where its frames are measured equal to software decoding, per codec and family; otherwise software decoding.
The tone map's curve is the one jellyscale sets in every family; no driver tone map.

Tested on real hardware in its own tier, chosen explicitly and never skipped: NVENC and AMD VAAPI on a developer machine; Octave (or, until JS-190 and JS-150, the native browser check) plays, seeks and recovers from a killed GPU worker.
Operators see the family and worker of each stream (Sessions, /metrics, JS-021 traces); the overrides are JS-170's three and no more.
An optional GPU worker pool requests nvidia.com/gpu or the vendor's resource through its device plugin; documented in docs/running.md.
source: PRODUCT.md phase5-library; rewritten 2026-11-08: the product owner wants every GPU and CPU in the cluster used where possible, priority kept in P5
notes: The dogfood cluster has an Intel iGPU on each of its three nodes (gpu.intel.com/i915: 1 allocatable) and the user's Jellyfin requests one; the developer machine has an RTX 4070 Ti and an AMD iGPU. GPU tone mapping (libplacebo or vendor filters) gives frames unlike zscale's, so it splices only within its own family. JS-154: the HD 530 cannot decode HEVC Main 10 or tone map in its video processor; software decode, OpenCL tone map and VAAPI encode reached 1.09x in a quiet pod, at 31 times x264's bytes at the bitrate tried. The UHD 630 nodes were measured by JS-163 and are JS-170's.
